newsitem.title: USA: Zaucha claims victory in Northstar vote.
newsitem.headline: Zaucha claims victory in Northstar vote.

text.p: Thomas Zaucha, who last month was dismissed as chief executive of Northstar Health Services Inc, on Monday said he was elected as its chairman, chief executive and president, winning 61 percent of the vote in a consent solicitation.
Telephone calls to the company's Indiana, Pennsylvania, headquarters went unanswered late Monday.
Zaucha was removed as chief executive after he began a proxy fight to remove the company's board.
In a release, Zaucha said Steven Brody, Robert Smallacombe and David Watson were removed from their executive positions and as board members.
In addition to Zaucha, new members of the company's board are Lawrence Jindra, James McElwain, Mark Mykityshyn, Roger Reschini and David White.
Zaucha said he would seek to convert all of the subordinated debt of the company that he holds into preferred or common equity.
He owns 949,958 shares of common stock in Northstar, and he holds $5.025 million of the company's notes, his spokesman, Mark Harnett, said.
